Area.evidence_source: The mother has another husband [mother had separated from Otunu's father] and Otunu had picked a quarrel the stepfather over an axe. The stepfather is still a strong and aggressive person, and Otunu feared him. Therefore, during that time his rate of drinking became very high, he could drink without eating". (case10:informant3) The initial quote denotes that the decedent was entrusted with money which he misappropriated through drinking. Possibly out of fear of the committee that assigned him the responsibility to keep the money and the fear of the son, he decided to kill himself to escape the shame of having abused that trust. Being a respectable member of the society, "a clan elder," and having betrayed the trust would have led to social embarrassment and might have been crucial for his decision to end his life (see Kizza, Knizek et al., in press). According to Möller-Leimkühler (2003), alcohol leads to "a reduction of selfesteem due to failure in social roles and relationships and can result in isolation and loss of support, which increases the risk of depression and suicide" (p. 4). The second quote indicates a person whose drinking strained his relationship with his family and parents. To finance his alcohol he used to sell property in the home, a state of affairs that attracted harsh treatment from significant others. The wife left him and the mother denied him access to food, so he could have felt abandoned. On this basis, he might have developed suicidal ideations and because of the disinhibiting effect of alcohol implemented the idea.
